schema_notes.is_historical_867: True if the barony name is contemporarily attested as a settlement, fortress, or administrative unit by <= 867 CE.
schema_notes.natural_proper_name: True if the barony name directly adopts a specific proper hydronym, oronym, choronym, or named topographic feature (excluding directional/locator compounds).
schema_notes.older_name_by_867: Records attested pre-867 CE names for the same site or immediate predecessor when distinct from the barony name.

b_oigon.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; saltwater lake in Zavkhan Province, Mongolia, documented in modern geographic and cartographic records.
b_oigon.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Ойгон нуур (Oigon nuur), referring to the saltwater lake in Zavkhan Province.

b_tsetsen_khairkhan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; mountain and sum in Zavkhan Province, Mongolia, documented in modern geographic and administrative records.
b_tsetsen_khairkhan.etymology_analysis: Mongolian honorific oronym Цэцэн хайрхан (Tsetsen Khairkhan, 'Wise Sacred Mountain'), associated with Tsetsen-Uul sum in Zavkhan Province.

b_tarvagatai.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; subrange of the Khangai Mountains in Zavkhan and Arkhangai provinces, Mongolia, documented in modern geographic records.
b_tarvagatai.etymology_analysis: Mongolian oronym Тарвагатай (Tarvagatai, 'abounding in marmots'), naming the Tarvagatai Nuruu range of the Khangai Mountains.

b_galt.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; sum (district) of Khövsgöl Province, Mongolia, documented in 20th-century administrative records.
b_galt.etymology_analysis: Mongolian place name Галт (Galt, literally 'with fire / fiery'), a sum in southern Khövsgöl Province.

b_tariat.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; the 8th-century Uyghur Tariat (Terkh) inscription is named after the modern sum rather than attesting the toponym 'Tariat' itself.
b_tariat.etymology_analysis: Mongolian toponym Тариат (Tariat, 'having grain/crops'), a sum in Arkhangai Province.

b_telmen.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; saltwater lake and sum in Zavkhan Province, Mongolia, documented in modern geographic records.

morphemes.translation: gentle-paced / ambling (horse gait, or proper lake name)

b_telmen.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Тэлмэн нуур (Telmen nuur), naming the saltwater lake in Zavkhan Province.

b_ikh_uul.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; sum (district) in Zavkhan Province, Mongolia, documented in modern administrative records.
b_ikh_uul.etymology_analysis: Mongolian compound Их-Уул (Ikh-Uul, 'Great Mountain'), a modern sum in Zavkhan Province.

b_sharga.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; sum (district) and desert basin in Govi-Altai Province, Mongolia, documented in modern geographic records.
b_sharga.etymology_analysis: Mongolian toponym Шарга (Sharga, 'pale yellow / bay'), naming the sum and adjacent Shargyn Gobi basin in Govi-Altai Province.

b_bumbag_hayrhan_uul.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; mountain in western Mongolia (Khovd/Govi-Altai region), documented in modern topographic maps.
b_bumbag_hayrhan_uul.etymology_analysis: Mongolian oronym Бумбаг Хайрхан уул (Bumbag Khairkhan Uul), combining 'vase/dome-shaped' with the honorific mountain title khairkhan and uul ('mountain').

b_tseel.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; sum (district) in Govi-Altai Province, Mongolia, documented in modern administrative records.

morphemes.translation: deep / clear / expansive (water or open space)

b_tseel.etymology_analysis: Mongolian toponym Цээл (Tseel, 'deep/clear/expansive'), a sum in Govi-Altai Province.

b_alag_khairkhan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; mountain in Bugat sum, Govi-Altai Province, Mongolia, protected as a natural monument in 1996.
b_alag_khairkhan.etymology_analysis: Mongolian oronym Алаг хайрхан (Alag Khairkhan, 'Variegated Sacred Mountain'), referring to the 3,783 m peak in Govi-Altai Province.

b_aj_bogd.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; branch mountain range of the Mongolian Altai in Govi-Altai Province, documented in modern geographic records.
b_aj_bogd.etymology_analysis: Mongolian oronym Аж Богд (Aj Bogd), a major branch range of the Mongolian Altai in Govi-Altai Province.

b_nutsgen_uul.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; mountain feature in western/southern Mongolia (audited for barony key b_nutsgen_uul rather than county-seat fallback Zarman).
b_nutsgen_uul.etymology_analysis: Mongolian oronym Нүцгэн уул (Nütsgen Uul, 'Bare Mountain'), referring to a treeless desert/steppe mountain.

b_eej_khairkhan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; sacred granite mountain in Tsogt sum, Govi-Altai Province, Mongolia, documented in modern geographic records.
b_eej_khairkhan.etymology_analysis: Mongolian honorific oronym Ээж хайрхан (Eej Khairkhan, 'Mother Sacred Mountain'), a natural monument in Govi-Altai Province.

b_zarman.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; semi-desert basin and oasis (Zakhui-Zarman Gobi) in Govi-Altai Province, Mongolia, documented in modern geographic records.
b_zarman.etymology_analysis: Mongolian topographic name Зарман (Zarman), designating the Zarman semi-desert oasis basin in Govi-Altai Province.

b_tofalaria.first_mention_attestation: Modern Russian/Soviet regional name (Tofalar National Region established in 1939 in Irkutsk Oblast; audited for barony key b_tofalaria rather than county-seat fallback Burugu Aallar).
b_tofalaria.etymology_analysis: Modern Russian choronym Тофалария (Tofalaria), formed from the Turkic ethnonym Tofalar (Tofa + plural -lar) with the Russian territorial suffix -iya.

older_name_by_867.notes: Chinese Sui and Tang chronicles record the Dubo (都播) in the Eastern Sayan region as the direct ancestors of the Tofalar and Tozhu Tuvan peoples.

b_miirchun.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; the Mirichun River (tributary of the Biryusa in Irkutsk Oblast) is first recorded in Russian gold-mining records from 1771.
b_miirchun.etymology_analysis: Siberian hydronym Миричун (Mirichun), a river and karst district in the Eastern Sayan highlands of Nizhneudinsky District, Irkutsk Oblast.

b_ikh_orgil.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; Mongolian descriptive compound ('Great Peak') used as a barony name in the Eastern Sayan/Tofalaria region.
b_ikh_orgil.etymology_analysis: Mongolian descriptive compound Их Оргил (Ikh Orgil, 'Great Peak').

b_kandat_uul.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; Kandat river and mountain area in the Sayan/Krasnoyarsk region, documented in modern Russian geographic records.
b_kandat_uul.etymology_analysis: Hybrid toponym combining the Siberian substrate name Kandat (attested in the Kandat River of Krasnoyarsk Krai) with Mongolian uul ('mountain').

b_kazyr.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; river in the Eastern Sayan Mountains (Irkutsk Oblast and Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russia), documented in modern Russian geographic records.
b_kazyr.etymology_analysis: Sayan Turkic hydronym Казыр (Kazyr, 'fierce / rapid'), describing the turbulent mountain river that joins the Amyl to form the Tuba.

b_kazas.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; Shor settlement and river in Kemerovo Oblast, southern Siberia, documented in modern Russian administrative records.
b_kazas.etymology_analysis: Southern Siberian toponym Казас (Kazas), naming a historical Shor settlement and tributary in Mountainous Shoria.

b_ergaki.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; mountain range in the Western Sayan Mountains, Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russia, documented in modern Russian geographic records.
b_ergaki.etymology_analysis: Sayan Turkic oronym Ергаки (Ergaki), traditionally linked to Tuvan ergek ('thumb / finger'), referring to the jagged granite spires of the Western Sayan range.

b_orgogdon_rok.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; unattested/synthetic CK3 barony name in the Sayan region without documented pre-867 historical records.
b_orgogdon_rok.etymology_analysis: Compound toponym combining Mongolian örgögdön ('uplifted/elevated') with rok ('rock').

b_baldyrgannyg.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; mountain ridge (Khrebet Baldyrgannyg) in the Sayan/Tuva region, documented in modern Russian topographic surveys.
b_baldyrgannyg.etymology_analysis: Tuvan oronym Балдырганныг (Baldyrgannyg, 'abounding in hogweed/angelica'), naming the Baldyrgannyg mountain ridge in southern Siberia.

b_kara_khol_TUV.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; lake and settlement in Bay-Tayginsky District, Tuva Republic, Russia, documented in modern geographic records.
b_kara_khol_TUV.etymology_analysis: Tuvan hydronym Кара-Хөл (Kara-Khöl, 'Black Lake'), referring to the dark reflection of the surrounding mountains on the lake's waters.

b_tsagaan_gazar.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; generic Mongolian descriptive term ('white/open treeless plain') without pre-867 documentary attestation.
b_tsagaan_gazar.etymology_analysis: Mongolian descriptive compound Цагаан газар (Tsagaan gazar, 'white/open land', meaning a flat, treeless steppe).

b_katu_yaryk.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; mountain pass descending into the Chulyshman River valley in the Altai Republic, Russia (modern road pass constructed 1987–1989).
b_katu_yaryk.etymology_analysis: Altai Turkic topographic name Кату-Ярык (Katu-Yaryk, 'Steep Gorge / Hard Cleft'), naming the dramatic pass into the Chulyshman valley.

b_altyn_kol.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; first documented in Russian Cossack expedition records from 1624–1633 and later cartography as Altin / Teletskoye.
b_altyn_kol.etymology_analysis: Altai Turkic hydronym Алтын Кӧл (Altyn-Köl, 'Golden Lake'), the indigenous name for Lake Teletskoye in the Altai Mountains.

b_darkhad.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; valley in northwestern Khövsgöl Province, Mongolia, named after the Darkhad Mongol subgroup (post-13th century).
b_darkhad.etymology_analysis: Mongolian toponym Дархад (Darkhad), plural of darkhan ('smith / tax-exempt'), naming the Darkhad people and the Darkhad Valley in Khövsgöl Province.

b_khoridol_saridag.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; 150 km mountain range between Lake Khövsgöl and the Darkhad Valley in Mongolia, documented in modern geographic records.
b_khoridol_saridag.etymology_analysis: Mongolian oronym Хорьдол Сарьдаг (Khoridol Saridag), combining the proper name Khoridol with saridag ('high bare mountain peak').

b_tsagaanuur.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; sum (district) in northwestern Khövsgöl Province, Mongolia, documented in 20th-century administrative records.
b_tsagaanuur.etymology_analysis: Mongolian compound Цагааннуур (Tsagaannuur, 'White Lake'), naming the sum in Khövsgöl Province.

b_tomorbulag.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; sum (district) in Khövsgöl Province, Mongolia, documented in 20th-century administrative records.
b_tomorbulag.etymology_analysis: Mongolian compound Төмөрбулаг (Tömörbulag, 'Iron Spring'), naming the sum in Khövsgöl Province.

b_karates.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; unattested/synthetic CK3 barony name in the Khövsgöl region without documented pre-867 historical records.
b_karates.etymology_analysis: Apparent Turkic-Mongolic compound (kara 'black' + tes, possibly referencing the Tes/Tez River basin), unattested as a historical settlement.

b_sangiin_dalai.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; saltwater lake on the border of Khövsgöl and Zavkhan provinces, Mongolia, documented in modern geographic records.
b_sangiin_dalai.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Сангийн далай (Sangiin Dalai, 'Treasury Ocean/Lake'), naming the large saltwater lake in northern Mongolia.

b_dood_tsagaan_nuur.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; lake in the Darkhad Valley, Khövsgöl Province, Mongolia (audited for barony key b_dood_tsagaan_nuur rather than county-seat fallback Ulantaiga).
b_dood_tsagaan_nuur.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Доод Цагаан нуур (Dood Tsagaan Nuur, 'Lower White Lake'), using the locator qualifier dood ('lower').

b_ulaantaiga.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; mountain range in northwestern Khövsgöl Province, Mongolia, documented in modern geographic records.
b_ulaantaiga.etymology_analysis: Mongolian oronym Улаан Тайга (Ulaan Taiga, 'Red Taiga'), naming the mountain range bordering the Darkhad Valley and Tuva.

b_bombogor.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; sum (district) in Bayankhongor Province, Mongolia, documented in 20th-century administrative records.
b_bombogor.etymology_analysis: Mongolian descriptive toponym Бөмбөгөр (Bömbögör, 'Dome / Rounded'), naming the sum in Bayankhongor Province.

b_boon_tsagaan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; large endorheic lake in Bayankhongor Province, Mongolia, documented in modern geographic records.
b_boon_tsagaan.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Бөөн Цагаан нуур (Böön Tsagaan Nuur, 'Mass White Lake'), naming the largest lake in the Valley of the Lakes.

b_khutag.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; Mongolian toponym ('blessed/sanctity') in the Bayankhongor/Gobi region without pre-867 documentary records.

b_gobi_gashunn.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; Gobi desert locality (audited for barony key b_gobi_gashunn rather than county-seat fallback Gurvan Saikhan).
b_gobi_gashunn.etymology_analysis: Mongolian descriptive compound Говь Гашуун (Govi Gashuun, 'Gobi Brackish [Spring/Basin]').

current_repo_state.name: Gurwan Sêchân
current_repo_state.b_anachronism: Authentic pre-867 indigenous physical toponym and territorial catchment (Gurwan Sêchân).

b_gobi_gurvan_saikhan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; mountain range ('Three Beauties of the Gobi') in Ömnögovi Province, Mongolia, documented in modern geographic records.
b_gobi_gurvan_saikhan.etymology_analysis: Mongolian oronym Говь Гурвансайхан (Govi Gurvansaikhan, 'Three Beauties of the Gobi'), referring to the eastern, middle, and western Saikhan subranges.

b_gobi_khatan_suudal.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; extinct volcanic peak and steppe locality in Bayankhongor Province, Mongolia, documented in modern geographic records.
b_gobi_khatan_suudal.etymology_analysis: Mongolian oronym Хатан Суудал (Khatan Suudal, 'Queen's Seat'), naming the volcanic outcrop and surrounding steppe in southern Mongolia.

b_ikh_bogd.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; highest mountain of the Gobi-Altai range in Bayankhongor Province, Mongolia, documented in modern geographic records.
b_ikh_bogd.etymology_analysis: Mongolian honorific oronym Их Богд (Ikh Bogd, 'Great Saint'), naming the 3,957 m summit of the Gobi-Altai Mountains.

current_repo_state.name: Ich Bogd
current_repo_state.b_anachronism: Authentic pre-867 indigenous physical toponym and territorial catchment (Ich Bogd).

b_tuin.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; river flowing south from the Khangai Mountains through Bayankhongor Province, Mongolia, documented in modern geographic records.
b_tuin.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Туйн гол (Tuin Gol), naming the river flowing past Bayankhongor into Orog Lake.

b_orog.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented as a saline lake in the Valley of the Lakes in modern Mongolian and Russian geographical literature.

morphemes.translation: orog (a proper lake name, possibly linked to Mongolian orog 'grayish/dun' or 'place/bed')

b_orog.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Orog nuur (Classical Mongolian: oroɣ naɣur), referring to the endorheic saline lake in Bogd sum, Bayankhongor Province, fed by the Tuin River.

b_khasagt_khairkhan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Mongolian geographical surveys as a major peak of the Gobi-Altai Mountains.

morphemes.translation: having wagons/carts or related to the Khoshot/Kazakh ethnonym
gracious/sacred (honorific term for a sacred mountain)

b_khasagt_khairkhan.etymology_analysis: Mongolian oronym Khasagt Khairkhan (Хасагт хайрхан), combining Khasagt with the reverential mountain epithet khairkhan ('gracious/sacred mountain').

b_gegeen.first_mention_attestation: Created in 2008 CE by the construction of the Taishir Hydro Power Station and dam on the Zavkhan River in Govi-Altai Province.
b_gegeen.etymology_analysis: Modern Mongolian name Gegeen nuur ('bright/holy lake'), given to the artificial reservoir formed in 2008 by the Taishir hydroelectric dam.

b_taigan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Mongolian geographical and limnological surveys in Govi-Altai Province.

morphemes.translation: taigan (proper name, possibly related to Turkic/Mongolic taiga 'mountain forest' or taigan 'sighthound')

b_taigan.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Taigan nuur, a saline tectonic lake in Govi-Altai Province, western Mongolia.

b_ongi.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE for the hydronym itself; the 8th-century Old Turkic Ongin inscription (c. 716–735 CE) was discovered near the river in 1891, but its text does not mention the name Ongi.
b_ongi.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Ongi gol (Онги гол), flowing from the southeastern Khangai Mountains through Övörkhangai and Dundgovi provinces.

current_repo_state.name: Ongî
current_repo_state.b_anachronism: Authentic pre-867 indigenous physical toponym and territorial catchment (Ongî).

b_taatsiin_tsagaan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Mongolian geographical and Ramsar wetland surveys.

morphemes.translation: of the Taats (genitive of Taats, the feeding river)

b_taatsiin_tsagaan.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Taatsiin Tsagaan nuur ('White Lake of the Taats [River]'), a saline lake in the Valley of the Lakes in Övörkhangai Province.

b_myangan_yamaat.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Mongolian topographic maps as the highest peak of Baga Bogd in Övörkhangai Province.
b_myangan_yamaat.etymology_analysis: Mongolian oronym Myangan Yamaat ('Having a Thousand Goats'), the highest summit (3,620 m) of the Baga Bogd massif in the Gobi-Altai range.

b_tovkhon.first_mention_attestation: Founded in 1653 CE by Zanabazar (originally called Bayasgalant Aglag Oron) upon his return from Tibet.
b_tovkhon.etymology_analysis: Mongolian monastery name Tövkhön khiid (Төвхөн хийд), established in 1653 CE in Övörkhangai Province as Zanabazar's mountain retreat.

current_repo_state.name: Tövchön
current_repo_state.b_anachronism: Authentic pre-867 indigenous physical toponym and territorial catchment (Tövchön).

b_guchin_us.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented as a modern sum (district) of Övörkhangai Province in Mongolia.
b_guchin_us.etymology_analysis: Mongolian toponym Guchin-Us (Гучин-Ус), literally 'Thirty Waters', referring to a sum (district) in southern Övörkhangai Province.

b_avraikheer.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Mongolian history as the capital of Övörkhangai Province.
b_avraikheer.etymology_analysis: Mongolian settlement name Arvaikheer (Арвайхээр, 'Barley Steppe'; rendered in-game/CK3 as Avraikheer), the capital of Övörkhangai Province.

b_khuisiin_naiman_nuur.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Mongolian geography as the Eight Lakes (Naiman Nuur) Nature Reserve in Khangai Nuruu National Park.
b_khuisiin_naiman_nuur.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Khuisiin Naiman Nuur (Хүйсийн Найман нуур, 'Eight Lakes of the Navel/Center'), a group of eight volcanic lakes in the Khangai Mountains.

b_khemchiq.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE for the Khemchik tributary itself (though the main Yenisei river is attested as Kem/Jian in 7th–8th century Chinese and Orkhon Turkic sources).

morphemes.translation: river (specifically the Yenisei, Old Turkic Käm)

b_khemchiq.etymology_analysis: Tuvan hydronym Khemchik (Хемчик, 'Little Khem / Little Yenisei'), formed from Tuvan khem ('river', cognate with Old Turkic Käm) plus the diminutive suffix -chik.

b_sagly.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; the Iron Age Sagly-Bazhy culture (5th–2nd centuries BCE) is named after the modern Tuvan locality of Sagly.

morphemes.translation: Sagly (toponym in Ovyursky Kozhuun, Western Tannu-Ola)

b_sagly.etymology_analysis: Tuvan toponym Sagly (Саглы), designating a village, river, and the highest summit (3,061 m) of the Western Tannu-Ola range in Tuva.

b_karatangdy.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; represents a CK3 compound/toponym combining Tuvan kara ('black') and Tangdy (Tannu-Ola).
b_karatangdy.etymology_analysis: Tuvan compound Kara-Tangdy ('Black Tannu-Ola'), combining kara ('black') and Tangdy ('high mountain', the Tuvan name of the Tannu-Ola range).

b_despen.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern geography as the highest peak (2,591 m) of the Eastern Tannu-Ola range and the Despen River valley in southern Tuva.

morphemes.translation: Despen (proper name of a peak and river in Eastern Tannu-Ola)

b_despen.etymology_analysis: Tuvan oronym and hydronym Despen, designating the highest point (2,591 m) of the Eastern Tannu-Ola mountains and its adjacent river valley in Tuva.

b_turgen_uul_bis.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Mongolian geography as a mountain range in the Uvs Lake Basin.
b_turgen_uul_bis.etymology_analysis: Mongolian oronym Türgen Uul (Түргэн уул, 'Swift Mountain'), a glaciated massif (3,965 m) in western Uvs Province.

b_mungun_taiga.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Russian and Tuvan geography as the highest massif in Tuva (3,970 m).
b_mungun_taiga.etymology_analysis: Tuvan oronym Möngün-Taiga (Мөңгүн-Тайга, 'Silver Mountain'), referring to the glaciated massif in southwestern Tuva.

b_khindigtik_khol.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Russian and Tuvan hydrographic registers as a glacial lake in Mongun-Tayginsky Kozhuun, Tuva.

morphemes.translation: having a navel (khindik 'navel' + -tig, referring to its central island)

b_khindigtik_khol.etymology_analysis: Tuvan hydronym Khindiktig-Khol (Хиндиктиг-Хөл, 'Lake with a Navel'), named for the prominent mountain island in the center of the lake.

b_tesiin_gol.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 759 CE as Old Turkic 'tez' (t(ä)z) in the Uyghur Shine Usu (Selenge Stone) inscription ('tez bašïnta', 'at the head of the Tez [River]'), and in the contemporaneous Tes inscription (c. 750–762 CE).

morphemes.translation: of the Tes (genitive of Tes, attested in Old Turkic as Tez)

b_tesiin_gol.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Tesiin gol (Тэсийн гол; Tuvan: Tes-Khem), continuing the Old Turkic river name Tez attested in 8th-century Uyghur runiform inscriptions.

b_bayan_UVS.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; generic Mongolian toponymic element Bayan ('rich') paired with the Uvs province identifier.
b_bayan_UVS.etymology_analysis: Mongolian toponymic element Bayan ('rich, abundant'), used in CK3 for a barony in the Uvs / Tesiin Gol region.

b_altan_els.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Mongolian geography as a sand dune massif in the Uvs Lake Basin.
b_altan_els.etymology_analysis: Mongolian topographic name Altan Els (Алтан элс, 'Golden Sands'), a protected sand dune region in the Uvs Lake Basin.

b_ulaangom.first_mention_attestation: Founded in 1686 CE (with late 17th-century grain cultivation and the 1871 Dechinravjaa Monastery).
b_ulaangom.etymology_analysis: Mongolian settlement name Ulaangom (Улаангом, 'Red Valley'), the capital of Uvs Province.

b_turgen.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented as a modern sum (district) of Uvs Province in western Mongolia.
b_turgen.etymology_analysis: Mongolian toponym Türgen (Түргэн, 'Swift'), designating a sum (district) in Uvs Province named after the nearby Türgen Uul / Türgen River.

b_khyarhgas.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE for the lake name itself (the lake is named after the Kyrgyz ethnonym, which is attested earlier, but the Mongolian hydronym Khyargas Nuur is post-867).
b_khyarhgas.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Khyargas (nuur) (Хяргас нуур), derived from the ethnonym Kyrgyz (Kirghiz), reflecting historical Kyrgyz presence in western Mongolia.

b_uvs_nuur.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in later Mongolian and Russian geographical sources as Mongolia's largest saline lake.

morphemes.translation: Uvs / Ubsu (from Mongolic übsün/subsen, bitter/saline sediment)

b_uvs_nuur.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Uvs nuur (Увс нуур; Classical Mongolian: ubsu naɣur), traditionally derived from a Mongolic word for the bitter sediment left in fermented mare's milk (airag), referring to the lake's high salinity.

b_khan_khokhii.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Mongolian geography as a sacred mountain range in Uvs Province.
b_khan_khokhii.etymology_analysis: Mongolian oronym Khan Khökhii (Хан хөхий), a sacred mountain range separating the Uvs Lake and Khyargas Lake basins in Uvs Province.

b_khan_huhiin.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; CK3 barony representing the genitive form (Khan Khökhiin) of the Khan Khökhii mountain range in Uvs Province.
b_khan_huhiin.etymology_analysis: Genitive form (Khan Khökhiin, Хан хөхийн) of the Mongolian oronym Khan Khökhii, used in phrases such as Khan Khökhiin nuruu ('Khan Khökhii Range').

b_gosudar.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; Russian common noun/title gosudar ('sovereign, ruler') used as a CK3 barony name in the Western Sayan.
b_gosudar.etymology_analysis: Russian title gosudar ('sovereign/lord'), appearing in early modern Russian-Siberian archival contexts and used as a barony key in CK3.

b_kantegir.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Russian and Khakas geographical sources as a left tributary of the Yenisei.

morphemes.translation: sky, heaven (cognate with Old Turkic täŋri)

b_kantegir.etymology_analysis: Russian adaptation (Кантегир) of Khakas Khan-Tigir (Хан-Тигір, 'Khan-Sky' or 'Heavenly Khan'), a mountain river in the Western Sayan flowing into the Yenisei.

b_sayanchu.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; CK3 barony name derived from the Sayan Mountains (Sayany).

morphemes.translation: Sayan (mountain range name, linked to the Soyan/Sayan tribe)

b_sayanchu.etymology_analysis: CK3 toponym Sayanchu, derived from the Sayan Mountains (Russian Sayany, Tuvan Sayan) in southern Siberia.

b_sutkhol.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Russian and Tuvan hydrographic registers as a mountain lake in Tuva.
b_sutkhol.etymology_analysis: Tuvan hydronym Süt-Khöl (Сүт-Хөл, 'Milk Lake'), a sacred alpine lake in the Western Sayan / Sut-Kholsky Kozhuun of Tuva.

b_stoyanka.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; Russian generic common noun stoyanka ('camp, halting place, archaeological site').
b_stoyanka.etymology_analysis: Russian common noun stoyanka ('camp, station'), commonly used in Siberian archaeology and topography for campsites and Paleolithic stations in the Western Sayan.

b_urbun.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Russian and Tuvan geographical sources as a left tributary of the Yenisei.

morphemes.translation: Urbun (proper name of a river and locality in Tuva)

b_urbun.etymology_analysis: Tuvan hydronym Urbun (Урбун), a mountain tributary of the Upper Yenisei in the Sayano-Shushensky Nature Reserve region of Tuva.

b_ulaan_gol.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Siberian/Sayan topographical sources as Ulan-Gol.
b_ulaan_gol.etymology_analysis: Mongolic hydronym Ulaan gol ('Red River'), attested in modern Russian cartography of the Sayan region as Ulan-Gol.

b_arja.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; while the Arzhan royal kurgans in Tuva date to the 9th–7th centuries BCE, the Tuvan toponym Arzhaan is modern.

morphemes.translation: mineral/medicinal spring (ultimately from Sanskrit rasāyana via Mongolic arshaan)

b_arja.etymology_analysis: CK3 rendering (Arja) of Tuvan Arzhaan (Аржаан, 'medicinal spring'), the name of a village and famous early Saka kurgan complex in Tuva.

b_khar_us.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Mongolian geography as a major freshwater lake in the Great Lakes Depression.
b_khar_us.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Khar-Us nuur (Хар-Ус нуур, 'Black Water Lake'), located in Khovd Province in the Great Lakes Depression of western Mongolia.

b_durgun.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Mongolian geography as a saltwater lake in Khovd Province.

morphemes.translation: Dörgön (proper lake name, also Russianized as Durgun)

b_durgun.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Dörgön nuur (Дөргөн нуур; Russianized as Durgun), a saline lake in the Great Lakes Depression of western Mongolia.

b_elsen_tasarkhai.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Mongolian geography as a sand dune belt.
b_elsen_tasarkhai.etymology_analysis: Mongolian topographic name Elsen Tasarkhai (Элсэн тасархай, 'Isolated Fragment of Sand'), referring to a strip of sand dunes amidst steppe.

b_uliastai.first_mention_attestation: Founded in 1733 CE as a Qing Manchu military garrison and administrative center for Outer Mongolia.
b_uliastai.etymology_analysis: Mongolian settlement name Uliastai (Улиастай, 'Place with Poplars'), founded in 1733 CE as the Qing military headquarters in western Mongolia.

b_ulaagchiin_khar.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Mongolian geography as a freshwater lake in Zavkhan Province.

morphemes.translation: of the red-coated/bay mare (genitive of ulaagchin)

b_ulaagchiin_khar.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Ulaagchinii Khar nuur (Улаагчны Хар нуур), a freshwater lake in Zavkhan Province bordered by sand dunes.

b_otgontenger.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Mongolian geography as the highest peak of the Khangai Mountains.
b_otgontenger.etymology_analysis: Mongolian oronym Otgontenger (Отгонтэнгэр, 'Youngest Sky'), the highest and only glaciated peak (4,021 m) of the Khangai Mountains in Zavkhan Province.

b_airag.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented in modern Mongolian geography as a freshwater lake in the Great Lakes Depression.
b_airag.etymology_analysis: Mongolian hydronym Airag nuur (Айраг нуур, 'Airag Lake'), a freshwater lake in the Great Lakes Depression connected to Khyargas Lake.

b_urgamal.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; documented as a modern sum (district) of Zavkhan Province in western Mongolia.
b_urgamal.etymology_analysis: Mongolian toponym Urgamal (Ургамал, 'Plant/Vegetation'), a sum (district) in western Zavkhan Province.

b_setsen_sart.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; derives from the Qing-era Khalkha Mongol banner Tsetsen Sartuulyn khoshuu ('Wise Sartuul's Banner') in Zavkhan Province.
b_setsen_sart.etymology_analysis: Mongolian banner/clan name Setsen Sart (from Qing-era Tsetsen Sartuulyn khoshuu, 'Wise Sartuul Banner'), associated with Zavkhan Province.
